title: Standard method for microCT-based additive manufacturing quality control 1: Porosity analysis
author: du Plessis, Sperling, et al.

steps.title: Build Ti‑6Al‑4V coupon
steps.instruction: Using a custom selective laser melting (SLM) platform inside a commercial LENS enclosure, fabricate a 10 × 10 × 10 mm Ti6Al4V coupon. Employ an IPG YLS 5000 ytterbium 5 kW fibre laser (λ = 1076 nm, fibre core = 50 µm) with an Intelliweld 30 FC V scanner. Feed gas‑atomized Ti6Al4V powder (particle size 20–60 µm) onto a Ti6Al4V base plate (≈150 mm diameter, ≈40 mm thick). Set hatch parameters to 3 kW power, 3 m s⁻¹ speed, 240 µm spot size. For contour scans use 1 kW laser power while varying hatch‑contour distance and speed to study density and surface finish. (For steels or heavier metals, increase voltage and apply stronger beam‑hardening correction during reconstruction.)

steps.title: Mount sample in foam
steps.instruction: Place the printed coupon in low‑density foam at an inclination of roughly 10–45° to avoid edge artefacts during scanning.

steps.title: Acquire microCT scan
steps.instruction: Scan the mounted sample on a laboratory microCT system with the following settings: 200 kV, 70 µA, 0.5 mm beam filter, 500 ms exposure per projection, 2400 projection steps over a full 360° rotation. At each step discard the first image and average the next two images. Total acquisition time is ≈1 h; including sample setup, machine warm‑up, background correction and reconstruction the whole process fits within ≈2 h.

steps.title: Reconstruct CT data
steps.instruction: Reconstruct the raw projection data using a strong beam‑hardening correction factor and **no** image de‑noising.

steps.title: Initial surface determination
steps.instruction: In VGStudioMax 3.1, apply the automatic surface determination to the whole volume and create a region of interest (ROI) from the detected surface.

steps.title: Close surface pores
steps.instruction: Apply an opening/closing morphological operation with a value of +3 to the ROI, then generate a new ROI that closes small surface pores caused by surface roughness.

steps.title: Select exterior air
steps.instruction: Use the region‑growing tool with high tolerance (grey‑value independent) on the air surrounding the part, selecting the option “avoid other visible ROIs”. Ensure the volume is highlighted and the ROI is visible; this selects all exterior air up to the surface defined by the previous ROI.

steps.title: Remove external noise particles
steps.instruction: If loose powder or other noise particles are present outside the part, apply another opening/closing (+3) operation to the exterior‑air region to eliminate them.

steps.title: Invert selection to obtain part volume
steps.instruction: Invert the exterior‑air selection; the resulting ROI now contains the entire part including all internal voids.

steps.title: Refine exterior surface
steps.instruction: Run a new advanced surface determination using the inverted ROI as the starting contour; this performs local optimisation for sub‑voxel surface precision.

steps.title: Create subsurface ROI
steps.instruction: From the refined surface ROI, use “select ROI from surface”, then switch to the “erode/dilate” mode and erode the ROI by ‑2 voxels (≈30 µm) to generate a subsurface ROI that excludes open edge pores.

steps.title: Extract subsurface volume
steps.instruction: Create a new volume from the eroded ROI and extract it for further defect analysis.

steps.title: Generate defect mask
steps.instruction: Apply an advanced surface determination to the material/defect interface within the extracted subsurface volume. Manually set the threshold in a well‑contrasted slice view (using the preview function) so that the boundary between pore space and material is correctly captured; if no pores are visible, set the threshold left of the material peak to obtain a zero result. Invert the thresholded region to isolate only void spaces. Use this inverted region as the defect mask for porosity analysis.

steps.title: Run porosity analysis
steps.instruction: Execute the porosity analysis function in VGStudioMax using the defect mask; the software will report total porosity, individual pore diameters (circumscribed sphere), and spatial distribution.

steps.title: Measure CT image quality
steps.instruction: Inside the 10 mm coupon select a 2.5 mm³ cube and compute its average grey value (GV) and standard deviation (σ). Calculate the material signal‑to‑noise ratio (SNRₘ = GV/σ). Repeat the same measurement in a background cube outside the part to obtain SNR_b. The ratio SNRₘ / SNR_b serves as an overall image‑quality metric. Perform this on the unprocessed reconstruction (no de‑noising).

steps.title: Assess pore proximity (gap distance)
steps.instruction: Define a 7 mm³ sub‑volume within the coupon (excluding near‑surface pores). For each detected pore compute its circumscribed‑sphere diameter and the gap distance to the nearest neighbouring pore (minimum centre‑to‑centre distance minus the two radii). Identify pores where gap distance < pore diameter; these fail the aerospace proximity criterion.
